correctness.rationale: Orthogonal Gaussian moments give the full analytic singular list; unitary Gaussian changes and a two-factor Mehler basis give the positive maximal list. For every p>0 the trace formulas follow by convergent geometric sums. The strict all-real-p order is proved via a derivative whose sign is determined by convex order of uniform distributions on nested symmetric intervals, including both equality exponents. Boundary profiles follow from exact multiplicity counts and uniform log-parameter expansions, and a Fourier multiplier gives the critical noncompact contrast. The packaged verifier reproduces an exact rational example and diagnostics but is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is the natural quantitative invariant for the same two Gaussian projections whose boundedness and compactness regions are known to agree. Its exact all-exponent reversal distinguishes kernel pointwise domination from singular-value geometry and identifies why Schatten p in (1,2) behaves oppositely to p>2 and p<1. It also supplies complete effective rank laws near the critical Gaussian balance, with different scaling functions despite the same compactness threshold. A generic theorem or a mere routine parameter variation is not being claimed.
